Android asks for this separately. Choose Allow all the time so an update can be sent about every 10 minutes while the app is closed. Without it, updates wait until you open the app.
Allowing unrestricted battery use keeps the 10-minute update closer to on time when the phone is asleep. It does not send any extra data.

This deletes the pairing and your partner\'s last location from this phone. Your name and photo stay on this phone. Sharing stops.
Loviedowpie is for you and one partner. There is no account, no analytics, and no ads. Location, battery, photos, and ring commands are encrypted so the relay cannot read them.
This is the same explanation as PRIVACY-DATA-FLOW.md.
Location, battery, your name, your photo, and ring commands leave the phone only as encrypted messages. They go to the relay, which stores ciphertext and cannot read it. Only your partner can.
The pairing code is shown on your screen. This app does not send the code. The relay sees a one-way id and the pairing handshake, not the code.
Encryption keys stay on the phone, wrapped by the Android keystore.
If wake-ups are set up, this phone\'s FCM token is sent to the relay so it can ask Google to ping you. The ping is empty. It has no location and no message.

When you open the map, tile images for the area on screen are downloaded from the OpenStreetMap tile server. That server sees the area you view and your IP address. It does not receive your partner\'s name, and it is not told that a coordinate belongs to them.
Update checks download a public version file and, if you ask, an APK from the relay. They contain no pairing data.
There is no analytics, no ads, and no account. The app does not ask for a phone number or an email address.
Relay messages expire on their own (about a day for messages, about 10 minutes for pairing).
